extracted.intended_audience: early-career computational scientists / postdoctoral candidates applying for the Damon Runyon Quantitative Biology Fellowship
extracted.subtask_description: Application, eligibility, selection, award terms, reporting, and financial rules for the Damon Runyon Quantitative Biology Fellowship Award—targeted to computational scientists seeking mentored postdoctoral training in cancer-related quantitative biology. Includes reviewer selection criteria and applicant/institutional obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of the applicant and career commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: The quality of the applicant, their commitment to pursuing a research career as a computational biologist, and the potential to excel in cancer research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate applicant qualifications, experience, productivity and demonstrated commitment to a research career in computational biology focused on cancer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity of the mentorship team
rubrics_metrics.description: The capacity of the mentorship team (two required) to provide a robust training experience that will accelerate the development of the applicant’s scientific skills and prepare them to independently conduct high quality, innovative cancer-related research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two mentors are required—one in a “dry lab” (computational) and one in a “wet lab” (cancer biology). Preference toward mentorship labs in close physical proximity to encourage frequent in-person meetings. Each Mentor must have generated a proven track record in the successful training of other scientists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifications, experience and productivity of applicant and mentors
rubrics_metrics.description: The qualifications, experience, and productivity of both the applicant and the Mentors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess prior productivity, relevant training, and evidence that mentors can support the applicant's development; mentors should demonstrate prior successful trainee outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of the research proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: The quality of the research proposal (importance of the problem, originality of approach, appropriateness of techniques and clarity of presentation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate problem significance, novelty of approach, suitability of methods, and how clearly the proposal is written and organized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Level of computational innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality of the level of computational innovation introduced to solve the proposed problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While building your own tools for analysis is not required, preference will be shown toward projects that create new or introduce novelty to existing technology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer awareness of unconscious bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are reminded to be aware of potential unconscious biases when reviewing, scoring and discussing candidates and applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At each review session a statement about unconscious bias is read aloud to reduce potential negative impacts on review outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required academic degree and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must have completed one or more of the following degrees or its equivalent: PhD, MD, MD/PhD, DDS, DVM, DO; must include a copy of their diploma to confirm date of conferral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the PhD diploma is not yet conferred but all requirements including defense are complete, submit a graduate school letter stating date of successful defense and date of degree conferral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentor and lab tenure restriction prior to application
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must not have been in their Mentors’ labs for more than 24 months prior to the application deadline date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement is intended to support applicants who are newly entering postdoctoral training with the proposed mentors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Level 1 eligibility (basic and physician-scientists pre-assistant professorship)
rubrics_metrics.description: Basic and physician-scientists must have received their degrees no more than five years prior to the application deadline date and may apply at any time prior to their initial assistant professorship appointment (or equivalent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must include diploma copy. Expected to devote 100% of their time to Damon Runyon-supported research activities. No other postdoctoral fellowships can be held concurrently. Candidates holding or awarded NIH K awards at the time of application are not eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Level 2 eligibility (physician-scientist specifics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Physician-scientist applicants must have completed residencies/clinical training, be board eligible in the United States at the fellowship start date, and be able to devote at least 80% of their time to Damon Runyon-supported research activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must not have had more than five years of postdoctoral laboratory research experience; may apply prior to initial assistant professorship; postdocs, clinical fellows, clinical instructors eligible. No concurrent postdoctoral fellowships; NIH K awards disqualify; institutional K12 award holders may apply but must turn-back K12 funding if awarded this fellowship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution and research location constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed research must be conducted at a university, hospital, or research institution. Foreign candidates may apply to do their research only in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates in structured postdoctoral research programs at for-profit institutions may apply; if awarded, the for-profit institution will pay salary and Damon Runyon will supplement if institutional salary is less than the Damon Runyon stipend. Candidates applying to foreign-based or U.S. government laboratories may be awarded a fellowship only if the program represents an unusual opportunity for postdoctoral training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discouragement of training in same institution/department as degree
rubrics_metrics.description: Postdoctoral training in the same institution in which the applicant received their degree is discouraged, particularly if it is in the same department.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applying to stay, the applicant must address reasons in their application. Proposals to continue training in the laboratory where the applicant received their PhD will not be considered. Proposals that are direct extensions of graduate work will not be funded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effort, concurrent awards and stipend supplementation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellowship award expectations on effort and concurrent support: Fellows are expected to devote specified percent effort (100% for basic Level 1; ≥80% for physician-scientists); no other postdoctoral fellowships may be held concurrently; candidates with NIH K awards are ineligible; institutional supplementation of stipend permitted but not other fellowship awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Total stipend should not exceed level of support for other professionals at same training level in that institution. Fellows may obtain additional awards/grants only to cover research expenses (not stipend). All current and pending support must be reported and relationships explained; budgetary overlap not allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: No pursuit of additional degrees during fellowship
rubrics_metrics.description: Damon Runyon Fellows are not permitted to pursue additional degrees during the course of their fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a condition of the award and must be adhered to throughout award period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award payment terms and institutional relationship
rubrics_metrics.description: All awards are made to the sponsoring institution for support of the designated Fellow and do not constitute an employer-employee relationship between the Foundation and the recipient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation will not modify its policies at individual institutional requests. Institutions must adhere to Foundation policies as approved by the Board of Directors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expense allowance rules and permitted uses
rubrics_metrics.description: A $2,000 expense allowance is awarded to the laboratory in which the Fellow is working and can be used by the Fellow for their educational and scientific expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: With written request, expense allowance may be used to defray cost of health benefits. Fellow determines spending with Mentor approval. Not for institutional overhead, postdoc registration fees or taxes. Institutions may not automatically deduct fees. Pre-award spending is not allowed. Contact Foundation for questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent Child Allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation will provide a Dependent Child Allowance of $1,000 per child per year (no allowance for a spouse).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligible Fellows must submit a dependent child allowance form and provide copy of birth or adoption certificate. Payment included in initial payment or in award year child is born/adopted and annually thereafter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical school loan repayment program eligibility and process
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation will retire up to $100,000 of qualifying medical school debt for awardees, paid over the three-year award period, subject to conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates must first apply to the NIH Loan Repayment Program to be eligible. Qualifying loans: tuition and direct educational expenses and interest; loans must be from government, academic, or commercial lending institutions. Documentation required within one month of acceptance and annually. Up to $33,333 per year paid directly to lenders. Consolidated loans require underlying loan agreements. Leave without pay generally suspends payments unless Foundation permission. If fellow terminates award early, they may be required to refund amounts unless they continue cancer research; Foundation determines tax reimbursement amount and may require payback schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality agreement restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows may not enter into confidentiality agreements that prevent or delay them from publishing and/or presenting their Damon Runyon-supported research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any agreements that would interfere with timely dissemination of research are prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific progress reporting requirements (interim reports)
rubrics_metrics.description: Second- and third-year funding is contingent upon satisfactory review of annual progress reports. At the end of the 11th and 23rd months, the Fellow must submit a detailed progress report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each interim report must include: a technical summary of research (technical but targeted to general scientific audience, ≤3 pages, signed by Fellow and Mentors), a lay abstract (≤1 page), bibliography of publications from award year (pdfs), request for OA fee reimbursement if applicable, list of conferences/seminars and presentations, brief description of collaborations and partners with affiliations, a brief summary from the Mentors assessing Fellow’s progress, completed intellectual property disclosure form, and expense allowance usage form for next year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final progress report requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: At the completion of the fellowship, the Fellow must submit a detailed final progress report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final report must include: a technical summary of research (≤3 pages, signed by Fellow and Mentors), two abstracts (one lay and one scientific), bibliography of all publications resulting from the research (pdfs), request for OA fee reimbursement if applicable, list of conferences/seminars and presentations, description of collaborations with affiliations, a statement indicating how the Damon Runyon award made a difference to the Fellow, a statement of future plans, up-to-date CV, a brief mentor summary assessing progress, and a completed intellectual property disclosure form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial reporting and account maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: The institution's financial officer must maintain a separate account including receipts for each fellowship, available for audit by the Foundation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports of expenditures on forms provided must be submitted within 60 days of the end of each award year. Unexpended expense allowance may carry over; unexpended stipend must be returned at year-end. Upon termination/expiration, final expenditures report and refund of unexpended balance must be submitted within 60 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial Expenditure Report preparation details
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed instructions for preparing the financial expenditure report for the expense allowance and allowable purchases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate carry-over of previous year’s expense allowance. If used for travel, provide meeting name/location, dates, and uses (registration, lodging, meals, transportation—coach class only for plane/train). For supplies, list general categories; equipment ≥$1,500 requires item name, date and price. 'Other' category only allowable for health insurance (if requested), scientific subscriptions, or items approved by the Foundation. Dependent Child Allowance must be reported as received but not how spent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publications and acknowledgments
rubrics_metrics.description: Publications and presentations resulting from Foundation-funded projects must carry a specific acknowledgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledgment text: "[Name of Awardee] is a Damon Runyon Fellow supported by the Damon Runyon Cancer Research Foundation (DRQ-[___])." Awardees should identify themselves as Damon Runyon Fellows at conferences and on websites and may use the Foundation logo as provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parental leave and notification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation will allow up to 12 weeks of paid parental leave for birth/adoptive parents consistent with the institution’s policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation must be notified in advance of the leave. Loan repayments will not be made during leaves of absence unless written permission is granted by the Foundation (applies to loan repayment program).

rubrics_metrics.name: Visa status and award continuation
rubrics_metrics.description: Host institutions must ensure awardees comply with federal immigration policy; the Foundation must be notified immediately if visa status changes or expires preventing work at the designated institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to notify may result in immediate termination of the award and may jeopardize future awards to the institution or Sponsor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modification, discontinuation or leaving institution requires approval
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Fellow and/or Mentor wish to discontinue the project, leave the designated institution or modify any aspect of the award, they must seek approval from the Damon Runyon Cancer Research Foundation in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to obtain approval may jeopardize future awards to the institution and/or Mentor by the Foundation.
